content: 1. To create an MLA Works Cited page, begin by typing the title Works Cited at the top of the page, centered, without italicizing or underlining the words. 2. Ensure that the page has one-inch margins on all sides, and use a readable font such as Times New Roman in 12-point size. 3. The Works Cited page should be the last page of your document and must include all sources that were directly cited in your paper. 4. Entries should be listed alphabetically by the author's last name. If no author is available, use the title of the work to determine its placement in the list. 5. For web documents or sources without page numbers, do not invent or include page numbers. Simply omit them. 6. Abbreviate the names of months in citations to reduce the length of entries, following MLA guidelines (e.g., Jan., Feb., Mar.). 7. When citing a single work with no author that is part of a collection, begin the entry with the title of the work, followed by the details of the collection. 8. The MLA Handbook, published by the Modern Language Association, serves as the authoritative guide for formatting and citing sources in MLA style. 9. If you wish to include works that you consulted but did not directly cite in your paper, you may create a separate section titled Works Consulted. 10. Use a hanging indent for each entry, where the first line is flush with the left margin, and subsequent lines are indented by half an inch. 11. When citing online sources, include the URL or DOI (if available) at the end of the citation. Ensure that the URL is not hyperlinked or underlined. 12. For formatting consistency, double-space all entries and do not add extra spaces between them. 13. If you are using a bibliography template or citation generator, verify that the output adheres to MLA standards before including it in your document. 14. The purpose of the Works Cited page is to provide clear and accurate documentation of all sources used, allowing readers to locate and verify the information.
